newsitem.title: CHINA: China domestic shares continue to plunge.
newsitem.headline: China domestic shares continue to plunge.

text.p: China's domestic A shares continued to fall on Friday on rumours that Beijing is drafting anti-speculation measures to follow up on Monday's market crackdown, brokers said.

The Shanghai A share index closed down 1.94 percent to 922.340 points, while Shenzhen A shares plunged 8.07 percent to 328.96 on turnover of 4.27 billion yuan compared with 7.33 billion yuan in the previous session.
But the foreign currency B shares on both markets fell only slightly due to bargain-hunting at low levels mainly on shares with strong earnings records, brokers said.
"Investors are just feeling their way at the moment," said HG Asia's Shanghai representative, Bruce Richardson. "But in general, medium and long-term sentiment is still very positive."
The Shanghai B index fell 0.600 points or 0.93 percent to 63.743 points, but off its intra-day low of 62.352 points.
On the Shenzhen market, the B index edged down 0.98 points or 0.78 percent to 125.56 on volume of 45.80 million shares worth HK$191.59 million against HK$472.61 million on Thursday.
"If there is no fresh market-moving news, the B share market will rally again next week," one broker said. "Few investors are willing to sell B shares any more at current cheap levels."
"Technical charts also indicate a rebound will come," he added.
Brokers in both markets said A share trading was affected by rumours that there could be negative market-moving announcements over the weekend, possibly including anti-speculation measures.
In Shenzhen, China Marine Container rose HK$0.27, or 3.55 percent, to HK$7.88 after 186,800 shares changed hands. The company had solid earnings in the past two years.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development, also a blue chip, traded the most, edging down $0.022 or 1.80 percent to $1.200, on volume of 3.5 million shares.
Brokers said the A share market is likely to fall further in the coming sessions with confidence badly hurt by the steep falls this week.

"The inflow of fresh money into A shares has been cut off by the People's Daily commentary published on Monday," a trader said. "Many domestic investors are disappointed at seeing their share prices diving nearly every day."
Many A shares, mainly cheap and smaller issues, have fallen by nearly 50 percent in the past seven sessions.
In Shenzhen, investors have scrambled to dump "rubbish stocks", shares in small firms with poor earnings records, brokers said.
Most such shares closed at the 10 percent limit-down level on Friday after they had been pushed to high levels by institutional punters in a bull run lasting from April to early this month.
